items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy: a pompous offended little town, then an exhausted deadpan island.
lines: Look at Spain's map. You're missing two neighbours.
And one of them is in Africa.
Everyone gets three: Portugal, France, and tiny Andorra.
Number four is British. Gibraltar, with a one point two kilometre land border.
Number five? Morocco. Two Spanish cities sit on the African coast, Say-oo-ta and Meh-lee-ya.
So Spain touches Africa three times.
The third is a rock a storm glued to Africa in nineteen thirty-four.
That border? Eighty-five metres. Shorter than a football pitch.
So if Spain spills into Africa... how is a Spanish town stuck inside France?
Rewind to sixteen fifty-nine. Spain hands France the villages of northern Ser-dahn-ya.
[pompous, offended] Village? Excuse me. I'm a town.
And towns weren't on the list.
So Lee-vee-ah stayed Spanish: thirteen square kilometres, about fifteen hundred people, surrounded by France.
Spain is one point six kilometres away. Close enough to wave.
And the treaty? Signed on a river island that still can't decide.
Pheasant Island is Spanish from February to July... then French until January.
[exhausted, deadpan] Six months each. I'm exhausted.
So... how many neighbours does Spain really have?
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
